notes: PSA 8.8 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.09. Prostate volume 98 mL. csPCa 0.62.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of a known prostate cancer diagnosis following a significant rise in serum prostate-specific antigen levels.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management, currently maintained on valsartan, lisinopril, and metoprolol for hypertension. The patient is a retired bank clerk who lives with his spouse and remains physically active, cycling approximately twenty kilometres twice weekly while consuming roughly one unit of alcohol per week. He reports minimal lower urinary tract symptoms, consistent with a mild IPSS score of 5, and denies any constitutional symptoms or bone pain. Recent healthcare encounters include a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins and a routine influenza vaccination administered by the practice nurse. His prostate-specific antigen trajectory has been notable, declining to 1.3 ng/mL in May of last year before sharply increasing to 8.8 ng/mL, with a calculated velocity of 0.46 ng/mL per year. He has no known drug allergies and continues his daily activities without limitation.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate gland is enlarged and symmetrically nodular without discrete focal induration or asymmetry, correlating with a clinical stage of cT1c. Vital signs are stable with a blood pressure of 130/89 mmHg and a heart rate of 66 beats per minute. General inspection reveals a well-nourished man in no acute distress, with clear lungs and a regular cardiac rhythm.
